olympics.text: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896.
Pierre de Coubertin of France founded the International Olympic Committee in 1894.
The five Olympic rings stand for the five inhabited continents joined together.
The ancient Olympics were held at Olympia, Greece, starting in 776 BC by tradition.
The first Winter Olympics were held in Chamonix, France, in 1924.
The Olympic flame is lit by the sun's rays at Olympia, Greece, before each Games.
The modern Olympic torch relay began at the 1936 Berlin Games.
Jesse Owens won four gold medals at the 1936 Berlin Olympics.
Michael Phelps won 8 gold medals at the 2008 Beijing Games, a record for one Olympics.
Michael Phelps won 28 Olympic medals, 23 of them gold, the most of any athlete.
Swimmer Mark Spitz won 7 gold medals at the 1972 Munich Olympics.
Nadia Comaneci scored the first perfect 10 in Olympic gymnastics in 1976.
In 1980 US college players beat the Soviet hockey team at Lake Placid: the Miracle on Ice.
The 1992 US basketball Dream Team had Michael Jordan, Magic Johnson and Larry Bird.
Usain Bolt won the 100 m and 200 m at three straight Olympics: 2008, 2012 and 2016.
Bob Beamon's 1968 long jump of 8.90 m stood as the world record for nearly 23 years.
Carl Lewis won the Olympic long jump four times in a row, 1984 to 1996.
Dick Fosbury won 1968 high jump gold going over the bar backward: the Fosbury Flop.
Jim Thorpe won the pentathlon and decathlon at the 1912 Stockholm Olympics.
Ethiopia's Abebe Bikila won the 1960 Olympic marathon running barefoot.
The marathon is 42.195 km (26.2 miles), the distance run at the 1908 London Games.
Muhammad Ali, then Cassius Clay, won boxing gold at the 1960 Rome Olympics.
Speed skater Eric Heiden won all five men's events at the 1980 Winter Olympics.
London is the only city to host the Summer Olympics three times: 1908, 1948, 2012.
Olympic gold medals are mostly silver, plated with at least 6 grams of gold.
Women first competed in the Olympics at the 1900 Paris Games.
The first Paralympic Games were held in Rome in 1960.
The Olympic motto is Citius, Altius, Fortius: Faster, Higher, Stronger.
At the opening ceremony Greece always marches in first, honoring the ancient Games.
Jamaica's bobsled team debuted at Calgary in 1988, inspiring the film Cool Runnings.
Norway's Sonja Henie won figure skating gold at three straight Olympics, 1928 to 1936.
Greg Louganis won both diving golds at the 1984 and 1988 Olympics.
The 1916, 1940 and 1944 Olympics were canceled because of the World Wars.
The Tokyo 2020 Olympics were held in 2021, delayed a year by the pandemic.
The US led a boycott of the 1980 Moscow Games; the Soviets skipped Los Angeles in 1984.
Soviet gymnast Larisa Latynina won 18 Olympic medals from 1956 to 1964.
The decathlon has 10 events over two days; its winner is often called the world's greatest athlete.
Lake Placid, New York, hosted the Winter Olympics in 1932 and 1980.
Los Angeles hosted the Summer Olympics in 1932 and 1984 and will again in 2028.
Kerri Strug landed a vault on an injured ankle to help the US win team gold in 1996.

nfl.text: The Green Bay Packers won Super Bowl I in January 1967, beating the Kansas City Chiefs.
The Super Bowl trophy is named for Packers coach Vince Lombardi.
The 1972 Miami Dolphins are the only NFL team to finish a full season and playoffs unbeaten.
The NFL was founded in 1920 in Canton, Ohio, as the American Professional Football Association.
The Pro Football Hall of Fame is in Canton, Ohio, where the league was born.
Joe Namath guaranteed a win before Super Bowl III, and his Jets upset the Colts.
Franco Harris's Immaculate Reception beat the Raiders in a 1972 playoff game.
Dwight Clark's leaping grab from Joe Montana, The Catch, sent the 49ers to the 1982 Super Bowl.
The 1967 NFL title game in Green Bay, the Ice Bowl, was played at 15 below zero.
The Green Bay Packers are owned by their fans, a rarity in US pro sports.
Chiefs owner Lamar Hunt suggested the name Super Bowl, inspired by a child's Super Ball.
Super Bowls use Roman numerals, except Super Bowl 50 in 2016.
An NFL field is 100 yards long plus two 10-yard end zones.
A touchdown is worth 6 points, a field goal 3 and a safety 2.
The NFL adopted the two-point conversion in 1994.
The NFL and the rival AFL merged in 1970, forming the AFC and NFC.
Walter Payton, Sweetness, was a Chicago Bears running back from 1975 to 1987.
Jim Brown led the NFL in rushing in 8 of his 9 seasons, then retired at 29 to act.
Jerry Rice holds the NFL career records for catches, receiving yards and touchdowns.
Tom Brady won seven Super Bowls, the most of any player.
Joe Montana won four Super Bowls with the 49ers and was never intercepted in one.
The Pittsburgh Steelers won four Super Bowls in six seasons, 1974 to 1979.
Monday Night Football first aired on ABC in 1970.
The Detroit Lions have played on Thanksgiving nearly every year since 1934.
The first NFL Draft was held in 1936. Jay Berwanger was the first pick.
Jay Berwanger, the first NFL draft pick, also won the first Heisman Trophy in 1935.
Vince Lombardi's Packers won the first two Super Bowls.
Don Shula has the most wins of any NFL head coach, 347.
The Buffalo Bills reached four straight Super Bowls, 1991 to 1994, and lost all four.
Scott Norwood's missed field goal in Super Bowl XXV became known as Wide Right.
The Los Angeles Rams were the first NFL team with a logo on their helmets, in 1948.
Dumping Gatorade on the winning coach became a tradition with the 1980s New York Giants.
Packers players celebrate touchdowns by jumping into the stands: the Lambeau Leap.
The 1985 Chicago Bears, with the Super Bowl Shuffle, won Super Bowl XX.
George Halas founded and coached the Chicago Bears. The NFC title trophy bears his name.
Brett Favre started 297 straight regular-season games at quarterback.
Roger Staubach coined Hail Mary for a desperate long pass after a 1975 playoff win.
The Music City Miracle was a 1999 playoff kickoff return by the Tennessee Titans.
The 1958 Colts-Giants title game, won in overtime, is called the Greatest Game Ever Played.
The Pro Bowl is the NFL's all-star game.

mlb.text: The 1869 Cincinnati Red Stockings were the first openly all-professional baseball team.
The first modern World Series was played in 1903; Boston beat Pittsburgh.
Babe Ruth hit 60 home runs in 1927, a record that stood for 34 years.
The Red Sox sold Babe Ruth to the Yankees in 1920, then waited 86 years for a title.
The 2004 Red Sox came back from 0-3 down against the Yankees, then won the World Series.
The Chicago Cubs won the 2016 World Series, their first title since 1908.
Jackie Robinson broke MLB's color line with the Brooklyn Dodgers in 1947.
MLB retired Jackie Robinson's number 42 for every team in 1997.
Lou Gehrig played 2,130 straight games and called himself the luckiest man on earth.
Cal Ripken Jr. broke Gehrig's streak in 1995 and ran it to 2,632 games.
Joe DiMaggio got a hit in 56 straight games in 1941, a record still standing.
Ted Williams hit .406 in 1941, the last major leaguer to hit .400.
Hank Aaron passed Babe Ruth with his 715th home run in 1974 and finished with 755.
Cy Young won 511 games, the most ever. Baseball's top pitching award bears his name.
Nolan Ryan threw seven no-hitters and struck out 5,714 batters, both records.
Don Larsen threw the only perfect game in World Series history in 1956.
Bobby Thomson's 1951 pennant-winning homer is called the Shot Heard 'Round the World.
The Baseball Hall of Fame in Cooperstown, New York, opened in 1939.
The first Hall of Fame class in 1936: Cobb, Ruth, Wagner, Mathewson and Johnson.
Ty Cobb has the highest career batting average in MLB history, about .367.
Pete Rose has the most hits in MLB history, 4,256.
Boston's Fenway Park opened in 1912 and is the oldest MLB ballpark still in use.
Fenway's 37-foot left field wall is called the Green Monster.
Ivy has covered Wrigley Field's outfield walls since 1937.
The first MLB night game was played in Cincinnati in 1935.
Take Me Out to the Ball Game was written in 1908 by men who had never seen a game.
The American League adopted the designated hitter in 1973; the NL followed in 2022.
Reggie Jackson hit three home runs on three pitches in Game 6 of the 1977 World Series.
Yogi Berra won 10 World Series rings as a player, the most ever.
The New York Yankees have won more World Series titles than any other team.
Dodgers lefty Sandy Koufax threw four no-hitters, including a perfect game in 1965.
Roberto Clemente's 3,000th hit in 1972 was the last regular-season hit of his career.
Willie Mays made The Catch, an over-the-shoulder grab, in the 1954 World Series.
Bill Mazeroski's 1960 homer won the World Series, the first to end a Game 7.
An injured Kirk Gibson hit a walk-off homer in Game 1 of the 1988 World Series.
The Miracle Mets went from last place to win the 1969 World Series.
A baseball has exactly 108 double stitches, sewn by hand.
The pitcher's mound is 60 feet, 6 inches from home plate, set in 1893.
A batting Triple Crown means leading the league in average, home runs and RBIs.
The All-American Girls Professional Baseball League ran from 1943 to 1954.

ufc.text: UFC 1 was held in Denver, Colorado, on November 12, 1993.
Royce Gracie won three of the first four UFC tournaments using Brazilian jiu-jitsu.
UFC fights take place in an eight-sided cage called the Octagon.
Dana White became UFC president in 2001 after the Fertitta brothers bought it.
Frank and Lorenzo Fertitta bought the UFC in 2001 for about $2 million.
The Ultimate Fighter reality show debuted in 2005 and helped make the UFC mainstream.
The 2005 Forrest Griffin vs Stephan Bonnar fight is credited with saving the UFC.
MMA's Unified Rules were first adopted by New Jersey's athletic commission in 2000.
UFC rounds last five minutes. Title fights go five rounds; most others go three.
Early UFC events had no weight classes; a big man could face a much smaller one.
Ronda Rousey was the UFC's first female champion, in 2012.
The first women's UFC fight was Ronda Rousey vs Liz Carmouche at UFC 157 in 2013.
Ronda Rousey won a judo bronze at the 2008 Olympics, the first for a US woman.
Anderson Silva defended the UFC middleweight title 10 times, 2006 to 2013.
Canada's Georges St-Pierre held UFC titles at welterweight and middleweight.
Chuck Liddell, The Iceman, was UFC light heavyweight champ and a Hall of Famer.
Randy Couture won UFC titles at heavyweight and light heavyweight.
The UFC Hall of Fame began in 2003 with Royce Gracie and Ken Shamrock.
Conor McGregor became the first UFC fighter to hold two titles at once, in 2016.
Conor McGregor knocked out Jose Aldo in 13 seconds at UFC 194 in 2015.
Amanda Nunes was the first woman to hold two UFC titles at the same time.
Khabib Nurmagomedov retired unbeaten at 29-0 as UFC lightweight champion.
Jon Jones became the youngest UFC champion at 23 in 2011.
Holly Holm, a boxing champion, knocked out Ronda Rousey with a head kick in 2015.
MMA stands for mixed martial arts: striking and grappling from many styles.
A UFC fight can end by knockout, submission or the judges' decision.
Fighters tap the mat or their opponent to submit and end the fight.
The rear-naked choke is one of the most common submissions in the UFC.
Most MMA fights are scored by three judges using the 10-point must system.
Japan's Pride FC was a big UFC rival until the UFC's owners bought it in 2007.
The UFC's parent company bought rival Strikeforce in 2011.
The UFC is based in Las Vegas, home of its Apex event center.
New York legalized pro MMA in 2016, the last US state to do so.
UFC 205 in 2016 was the first UFC event at Madison Square Garden.
The UFC's first network TV event aired on Fox in 2011.
The Gracie family developed Brazilian jiu-jitsu from judo in the early 1900s.
UFC fighters wear 4-ounce open-finger gloves so they can grapple.
Ken Shamrock was the first UFC Superfight champion, in 1995.
UFC president Dana White has called Bruce Lee the father of mixed martial arts.
UFC pays bonuses for Fight of the Night and Performance of the Night.
